column2: On the authority of Abū Muḥammad ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “None of you truly believes until his inclination follows what I have brought.” An authentic hadith; we have narrated it in Kitāb al-Ḥujjah with an authentic chain.
Al-Nawawī graded the hadith authentic and attributed it to Kitāb al-Ḥujjah. Ibn Rajab said in Jāmiʿ al-ʿUlūm wa-l-Ḥikam (2/293):

“By the author of Kitāb al-Ḥujjah he means Shaykh Abū al-Fatḥ Naṣr ibn Ibrāhīm al-Maqdisī al-Shāfiʿī, the jurist and ascetic who settled in Damascus. This book of his is Kitāb al-Ḥujjah ʿalā Tārikī al-Maḥajjah,
which sets out the fundamentals of the religion according to the principles of the people of hadith and Sunnah.

The ḥāfiẓ Abū Nuʿaym recorded this hadith in his Kitāb al-Arbaʿīn, stipulating at its beginning that [its hadiths] would be from the authentic reports and sound narrations whose transmitters are agreed to be upright, and the imams have recorded it in their Musnads.”
Then the ḥāfiẓ Ibn Rajab declared it weak and explained the reasons for its weakness. As for the ḥāfiẓ Ibn Ḥajar, he indicated in al-Fatḥ (13/289) that it is established,
attributing it to the hadith of Abū Hurayrah. He said: “Al-Bayhaqī in al-Madkhal and Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr in Bayān al-ʿIlm recorded from a number of the Successors,

such as al-Ḥasan, Ibn Sīrīn, Shurayḥ, al-Shaʿbī and al-Nakhaʿī, statements with good chains censuring speaking on the basis of mere opinion. All of that is gathered in the hadith of Abū Hurayrah, ‘None of you truly believes until his inclination follows what I have brought’,
recorded by al-Ḥasan ibn Sufyān and others; its narrators are trustworthy, and al-Nawawī declared it authentic at the end of the Forty.”

The negation of faith in the hadith denies the completeness of faith that is obligatory. Al-Nawawī said in his commentary on the Forty: “That is, a person must measure his deeds against the Book and the Sunnah, oppose his inclination and follow what he ﷺ brought.

This is like the words of the Exalted: ‘It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any choice in their matter’ [al-Aḥzāb 33:36]. No one has any say or inclination alongside Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and His Messenger ﷺ.”

Ibn Rajab said in Jāmiʿ al-ʿUlūm wa-l-Ḥikam (2/398–399): “The well-known use of hawā (inclination), when used without qualification, is inclination towards what is contrary to the truth, as in the words of the Mighty and Majestic: ‘And do not follow [your] inclination, lest it lead you astray from the path of Allah’ [Ṣād 38:26]; and the Exalted said:

‘But as for one who feared standing before his Lord and restrained the soul from [unlawful] inclination, then indeed Paradise will be [his] refuge’ [al-Nāziʿāt 79:40–41]. Hawā is also used in the sense of love and inclination in general, which includes inclination towards the truth and other things;
and it may be used specifically in the sense of loving the truth and submitting to it. Ṣafwān ibn ʿAssāl was asked: Did you hear the Prophet ﷺ mention hawā?
He said: A Bedouin asked him about a man who loves a people but has not caught up with them,

and he said: ‘A person will be with those he loves.’ And when the words of the Mighty and Majestic were revealed, ‘You may defer whom you will of them and take to yourself whom you will’ [al-Aḥzāb 33:51], ʿĀʾishah said to the Prophet ﷺ:
‘I see that your Lord hastens to fulfil your wish (hawāk).’ And ʿUmar said in the story of the consultation about the captives of Badr:
‘The Messenger of Allah ﷺ inclined (hawiya) to what Abū Bakr said, and did not incline to what I said.’ This hadith is among those in which hawā is used in the sense of praiseworthy love.”
The Messenger ﷺ must be followed in what he brought.
People vary in the degree of their faith.
